regulatory_context.pdt_note: SEC approved removal of the $25,000 PDT minimum on 2026-04-14; FINRA set 2026-06-04 as the effective date. The $25k equity floor, the 4-trades-in-5-days counter and the 90-day freeze are gone, replaced by a risk-based intraday margin framework. Broker-dealers have an 18-month phase-in, so HOUSE requirements still vary -- confirm with the broker before sizing.
regulatory_context.consequence: The T+1 cash-account capital-partition model (fixed $4,000 per trade, risk cut to 0.20-0.50%) that one research source built the plan around is obsolete. On a margin account, size on RISK, not on settled-cash partitions.

items.headline: US military destroyed/disabled three Iranian oil tankers after IRGC fired ballistic missiles at two US Navy warships (an aircraft carrier was targeted)
items.detail: CENTCOM 'permanently disabled' two tankers and 'completely destroyed' a third, describing them as part of a multibillion-dollar shadow fleet funding the IRGC and its proxies. CENTCOM warned it will destroy Tehran's oil fleet if necessary. Strikes hit in the Gulf of Oman and near Kharg Island.

items.headline: Strait of Hormuz effectively closed to commercial shipping -- 6 transits recorded against a baseline of 85/day
items.detail: Closed to routine commercial traffic since 2026-07-30 after a June US-Iran agreement broke down. ~25% of seaborne oil and ~20% of LNG normally transit it. Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM and Hapag-Lloyd have suspended transits; 150+ tankers anchored outside. Iran's parliament speaker says its forces control the strait and will not allow it reopened.
items.note: This is a continuing condition, not a weekend event. It is the backdrop the tanker strikes escalated, not a fresh catalyst -- do not double-count it.

items.headline: WTI around $91, Brent around $95-96, roughly +$5 since hostilities renewed
items.detail: Sources disagree on the exact post-strike print and one undated headline suggests WTI toward $105. Treat oil as ELEVATED and TRENDING UP with a wide error bar; do not trade off a specific level quoted here.

items.headline: Nvidia CONFIRMED the Hugging Face acquisition at $12.93B
items.detail: ~$11.9B to shareholders plus up to $1B in equity retention. Expected to close in H1 2027, PENDING REGULATORY APPROVAL. This is the catalyst behind Friday's AI-complex bid (CBRS +12%).
items.caveat: Regulatory approval is not granted. A confirmed deal that still needs clearance is a headline risk in both directions, not a settled fact.

items.headline: Broadcom fiscal Q3 AI semiconductor revenue $16.7B, +221% YoY and +54% sequentially
items.detail: The AI-capex thesis is intact at the fundamental level even though AVGO's stock fell ~3% on the print. Fundamentals and price action point opposite ways here -- the price action is what you trade.

items.headline: TrendForce sees NAND prices +10-15% this quarter, down from an estimated ~70% jump SanDisk just rode
items.detail: Still-positive pricing, but a sharp DECELERATION in the rate of change -- which is what a momentum trade is actually long. Micron flags tight NAND/DRAM beyond 2027; 2026 DRAM revenue projected +246.6% and NAND +371.9%. Structural risk: YMTC and CXMT capacity expansion could pressure prices.

items.headline: September rate-HIKE odds rose after the payrolls beat; sources put them roughly 48-58%
items.detail: CME FedWatch cited near 56% for a 25bp hike, Kalshi 48%, Polymarket 49%, and one post-payrolls read 58%. Before Warsh's remarks, a hold was near 70%. Sources disagree and are dated differently -- treat this as a coin flip, not a known number.

weekend_developments.net_read: Friday was a single-driver tape: hawkish payrolls, yields up, indices down, semis up on relative strength. Tuesday opens with a SECOND driver stacked on it -- a weekend military escalation with oil elevated and Hormuz shut. Higher oil feeds the inflation print that lands Friday, which feeds the hike the FOMC decides the following week. That chain is a headwind for exactly the high-multiple growth names that dominate this watchlist, at the same time as it is a tailwind for the gold names at the top of the ranking. The two halves of this list now point in opposite directions, and that is the single most important change since Friday's close.
